question.prompt:
Squares of side length \(1,\) \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) and \(5\) are arranged to form the rectangle shown below. A curve is drawn by inscribing a quarter circle in each square and joining the quarter circles in order, from shortest to longest. What is the length of the curve?

[Figure 1](figures/2026_AMC_8_Q11_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Each drawn quarter circle has two sides of its square as radii, so its radius equals the square's side length.

A circle of radius \(r>0\) has circumference \(2\pi r\). A quarter circle has one fourth of that length:
\[
\frac14(2\pi r)=\frac{\pi r}{2}.
\]
The five arcs join at their endpoints, so their lengths add. Their radii are \(1,1,2,3,5\), giving a total length of
\[
\frac{\pi}{2}(1+1+2+3+5)
=\frac{\pi}{2}\cdot12
=\boxed{6\pi}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Add quarter circumferences
